questions.q: Which point is equidistant from O(0,0,0), A(l,0,0), B(0,m,0) and C(0,0,n)?
questions.explanation: Let the point be (x,y,z) and equate its squared distance from O with its squared distance from A. This gives x=l/2; similarly comparison with B and C gives y=m/2 and z=n/2. Hence the required point is (l/2,m/2,n/2).

questions.q: Find the point on the x-axis that is equidistant from A(3,2,2) and B(5,5,4).
questions.explanation: A point on the x-axis has the form P(x,0,0). Equating PA^2 and PB^2 gives (x-3)^2+4+4=(x-5)^2+25+16. Simplification yields 4x=49, so P=(49/4,0,0).

questions.q: In what ratio does the xz-plane divide the line segment joining P(2,4,5) and Q(3,5,-4)?
questions.explanation: Let the dividing ratio be k:1 and apply the section formula to the y-coordinate. Because every point on the xz-plane has y=0, (5k+4)/(k+1)=0, giving k=-4/5. The negative sign indicates external division, with magnitude ratio 4:5.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, A=(3,2,0), B=(5,3,2), C=(-9,6,-3). The internal angle bisector from A meets BC at D. What are the coordinates of D?
questions.explanation: First compute AB=3 and AC=13. By the angle-bisector theorem, D divides BC internally in the ratio BD:DC=3:13. Applying the 3D section formula gives D=(19/8,57/16,17/16).
